feed.title: Former Tesla President Says Car Sales Are Funding the Longer Road to Robots and Cybercabs
feed.summary: Former Tesla President Jon McNeill states that Tesla's traditional car sales are crucial for funding its long-term ambitions in robotaxis and humanoid robots, which require extensive capital and development time. McNeill also noted that prediction market traders were more accurate than Wall Street analysts in forecasting Tesla's recent delivery numbers.

feed.title: Aevex Corp. (AVEX) Shareholders Who Lost Money Have Opportunity to Lead Securities Fraud Lawsuit
feed.summary: Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP has announced a securities fraud class action lawsuit against Aevex Corp. (AVEX), inviting shareholders who suffered losses to become lead plaintiffs. The lawsuit alleges that Aevex and certain underwriters made false statements between April 14, 2026, and June 4, 2026, by failing to disclose a pre-arranged plan to abrogate a lock-up and conduct a secondary public offering (SPO) shortly after the IPO, where all proceeds went to Madison, not Aevex. Investors have until October 20, 2026, to move to be appointed lead plaintiff.

feed.title: McDonald's 30% Slide Has Made It Cheaper, but Traffic Is Still the Problem
feed.summary: McDonald's stock has dropped over 30% from its February peak, making its valuation and dividend yield more attractive, but affordability concerns and changing consumer habits are impacting traffic. The company is facing challenges with higher costs and the potential long-term effects of GLP-1 medications on fast-food spending. McDonald's new strategy, NEXT, aims to improve restaurant economics and efficiency, with visitor traffic being the key metric to watch for a successful rebound.

feed.title: Costco faces federal lawsuit accusing retailer of selling products linked to child and forced labor
feed.summary: Costco is facing a federal class-action lawsuit in Oregon, alleging the retailer sells products sourced from child and forced labor. The lawsuit claims chocolate, cashews, and shrimp sold by Costco are linked to exploitation in West Africa, Brazil, Vietnam, Guinea-Bissau, and India. The suit seeks $200 for each eligible Oregon Costco member and an injunction to halt the company's "unlawful" business practices, highlighting Costco's marketing as an "ethically sourced" retailer.

feed.title: John Deere Financial, AgVend Bring 0% & Low Rate Crop Input Financing into Retail Quote
feed.summary: John Deere Financial and AgVend have partnered to integrate 0% and low-rate crop input financing directly into retailers' AgVend platforms, making these offers visible during planning, quoting, and ordering. This initiative aims to provide growers with alternative lending options, allowing them to finance seed and crop protection purchases until November 2027, countering higher operating line interest rates. The integration also benefits retailers by taking on the financial risk and processing, functioning as an account receivable replacement tool.

Nedzbala, who joined GDIT via the CSRA acquisition, was previously the chief business officer.

feed.title: Starbucks loses bid to dismiss labor union's trademark case
feed.summary: A federal judge in Pennsylvania has denied Starbucks' request to dismiss a lawsuit filed by Workers United, the union representing thousands of its employees. The union's lawsuit aims to validate its use of the name "Starbucks Workers United" and a modified Starbucks logo, in response to the coffee giant's trademark infringement claims. This legal dispute is part of ongoing tensions between Starbucks and the union that began five years ago when the first employees unionized.

This marks the first time in 30 years the property has changed ownership. The Summit, established in 1997, has grown into an 870,000-square-foot retail destination.

feed.title: Realty Income Rewarded Patient Investors Over Ten Years but Recent Buyers Face a Steep Decline
feed.summary: Realty Income (NYSE: O) has significantly underperformed the S&P 500 over the past decade, returning only 33% with reinvested dividends compared to the S&P 500's 314% gain. While its consistent monthly dividends have turned a price loss into a modest gain for long-term holders, recent buyers face a steep decline due to rising Treasury yields. The company has expanded its global property portfolio and increased its dividend, but its future performance largely depends on long-term interest rates.

feed.title: Certified recycled plastic could reduce exposure to oil-price swings
feed.summary: SMX (Security Matters) PLC suggests that certified recycled plastic can be an economic alternative to virgin plastic, especially amidst global supply risks, oil price volatility, and geopolitical instability. The company's molecular marking technology helps verify the origin and content of recycled materials, transforming them into a valuable, verifiable asset that can compete with traditional oil-derived plastics on cost-efficiency rather than just environmental benefits. This approach aims to provide industrial resilience against material shortages and price shocks.

feed.title: All In On McDonald's Stock? Social Media User Wants Advice on Fast Food Giant, Investors Aren't Lovin' It
feed.summary: A social media user, Nik Hulewsky, sought advice on whether to invest his entire net worth in McDonald's (NYSE: MCD) stock, citing a 3.3% dividend yield and perceived low valuation. Investor responses largely expressed skepticism due to changing consumer tastes, high McDonald's prices, and the impact of weight-loss drugs, leading Hulewsky to purchase only 10 shares instead of going "all in."

feed.title: Ford Sales Slide 6.6% After Model Phase-Outs
feed.summary: Ford Motor Company reported a 6.6% year-over-year decline in third-quarter U.S. vehicle sales, primarily due to planned phase-outs of the Escape and Lincoln Corsair models. Despite the overall sales dip, Ford estimated an increase in its retail market share to 12.1% when excluding the phased-out models. The company saw strong performance in its F-Series trucks, Maverick Hybrid, and Bronco sales, and maintained its adjusted EBIT guidance for 2026 despite a short-term supplier issue affecting F-150 production.
